sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1976. Austronesian languages: Sepik Provinces. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study vol. 2, 399-418. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.note: Sepa entry: 'Spoken in the two mainland villages of Sepa and Wanam, opposite Manam Island, by approximately 265 people; very closely related to Manam, according to Z'graggen (1971)'; comparative wordlist rows only; no stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.note: Sepa appears only in cognate-percentage tables. General note on transcription (pp. 13-14): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Nothing Sepa-specific.

sources.citation: de.wikipedia, 'Josef Schebesta' (SVD missionary at Bogia 1913-1942)
sources.note: States that besides Anthropos articles he 'verfasste eine Grammatik und Wörterbücher der Lokalsprachen' (wrote a grammar and dictionaries of the local languages) — apparently unpublished manuscripts; dates the WZKM Sepa texts to vol. 38 (1931), pp. 249-262.

sources.note: Lists no grammar, grammar sketch, phonology or dictionary for Sepa; the seven hh.bib entries coded [spe] are Ross 1988, Z'graggen 1968/1969/1975, Laycock 1973/1976 (overview/comparative/wordlist) and Schebesta 1932 (text). Subclassification refs Lichtenberk 1983, Ross 1988; comment Z'graggen 1969:189.

sources.note: Sepa appears only as a Schouten-chain data language (wordlists, sound correspondences). The only stress remarks (example 3.115 and discussion) concern Ali and Tumleo verb stress alternations; nothing on Sepa stress.

sources.note: Classifies the 'Meseman' languages (Manam-Sepa-Medebur) and gives Sepa rows in comparative wordlists; no phonology, no stress.

sources.note: Village/census listings for Sepa and Wanam and a bibliography naming Schebesta's Sepa publications (1921-22 Anthropos 16/17: 1053-5; 1932 WZKM 38: 249-62; 1938 Anthropos 33: 659-63). No phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sepa entry: 'All data from Z'graggen (1971). According to Z'graggen, Sepa shares 72% cognates with Manam, and could therefore be regarded as a dialect of it; however, indigenous opinion is firm that it should be regarded as a separate language'. No phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: The published version of the 1969 thesis and Laycock's sole data source for Sepa (pronouns, cognate percentages); should be checked in case the printed version adds a phonological note, though the thesis omits stress marking throughout.

sources.citation: Höltker, Georg. 1947. Die maritime Ortung bei einigen Stämmen in Nordost-Neuguinea. Geographica Helvetica 2(3): 192-205. doi:10.5194/gh-2-192-1947
sources.note: No phonology content. The Sepa-Wanami section gives migration history (from Manam four or five generations earlier; 194 people in 1936), states that they speak a dialect of Manam, and lists direction terms with word-class notes: otianga 'Osten / das Gehen nach Osten', oti 'nach Osten gehen', oleanga/olo 'Westen', lakonga/lako 'Sueden oder Norden', sopu 'herkommen'; footnote: 'Das olo der Sepa-Wanami und das gleichbedeutende oro der Manam sind nur dialektisch verschieden'. No stress/accent marks on the forms and no remark on Betonung, Akzent, Ton or Silbe anywhere in the article (a full-text s…

sources.citation: Hoeltker, Georg. 1942-45. [Nachruf:] P. Josef Schebesta, S.V.D. (1885-1944). Anthropos 37-40 (Analecta et Additamenta): c. 881-883.
sources.note: No phonology content. Documents that (a) Schebesta's field notes were copied by Hoeltker 1936-39 and survive (to appear in Hoeltker's Bogia monographs), (b) the Sepa-Grammatik MS was destroyed at Bogia in WWII and Hoeltker holds no copy, (c) Dempwolff (Hamburg, d. 1938) had edited it for print -- so the only conceivable surviving trace would be in Dempwolff's papers (Universitaet Hamburg), unverified. Also lists Schebesta's complete published output on Sepa (1913, 1921-22a/b, 1932, 1938, 1940-41).

sources.citation: Hoeltker, Georg. 1940-41. Verstreute ethnographische Notizen ueber Neuguinea (Eine Sammlung aus den ersten Jahrgaengen des 'Steyler Missionsbote'). Anthropos 35-36: 1-67 [section 'Bogia (einschliesslich: Sepa-Wanami)', pp. 49-52]; with W. Schmidt, review/announcement, ibid. pp. 506-507.
sources.note: No phonology. Ethnographic/mission notes: 'die Wanami haben mit den Sepa dieselbe Sprache.. eine Sepa-Wanami-Grammatik ist im Entstehen.. in der Schule wird Sepa gesprochen'; 'Sepa ist leicht zu erlernen'; Sepa c. 250-350 people in three villages (1902-04). P. 507 (W. Schmidt) announces as Ergaenzungsband III zur Ethnographie Neuguineas: 'J. Schebesta und G. Hoeltker, Die Sepa-Wanami, zwei melanesische Staemme am Bogia-Hafen' (manuscript said to exist in 1941; never published -- Hoeltker papers, Anthropos-Institut Sankt Augustin, would be the place to look).

sources.citation: Schebesta, Josef. 1938. Ein Versuch, der aeltesten Gottheit der Sepa in Neuguinea auf linguistischem Wege naeherzukommen. Anthropos 33: 659-663.
sources.note: Etymological-mythological note: a Sepa yam-magic spell with interlinear gloss, Sepa phrases (Kiaro isonomiko, Kiaro isami, guau-dzama), remarks on genitive order (older postposed vs. modern preposed genitive), sound correspondences n~l, r~l, prenasalisation ('Einfuegung eines m vor b'), a note that Wogeo and Biem favour consonant-final words; comparisons with Manam, Wanami, Wogeo, Tumleo, Murik etc. Nothing on Betonung/Akzent or tone. Refers repeatedly to a 'Sepa-Monographie' in preparation (never published).

sources.citation: Lichtenberk, Frantisek. 1983. A grammar of Manam. Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 18. Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Full grammar of Manam, the sister language sharing 72% cognates with Sepa (Laycock 1973); gives a detailed Manam stress rule and is the closest available proxy, but it describes Manam, not Sepa — usable only as an identity/proxy note, never as a Sepa statement.
